title: Refine the marking guide on real answers
statement: Refine a marking guide against real student answers before relying on it, rather than writing it in one pass.
detail: A grading study summarised in the AP question work (Grade Like a Human) runs marking-guide generation, grading and post-grading review, and treats writing the guide as an optimisation problem rather than a single pass (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_educational_content_generation.md`). It found guides tuned on actual student answers more accurate and reliable. The summary gives no figures, the paper was not opened, and the project never tried it.
against: The cited work treats marking guides as scoring tools and doesn't test the facts inside them: "Most work treats rubrics as frozen artifacts used for scoring, not as generated content that must be historically accurate." (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_educational_content_generation.md`, line 75).

evidence.quote: - Relevant insight: rubrics optimized against actual student answers are more accurate and reliable
- **The key technique:** rubric generation as an optimization problem, not a single-shot generation

citations.ref: Grade Like a Human: Rethinking Automated Assessment with LLMs (arXiv:2405.19694)
